items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: this guy came to Chicago and did some records he made with Gene Adler‟s father

ctx.x: Talking about Guy Kelly, this great trumpet player. He‟s from Baton Rouge. Now he‟s darker. He had lots of bumps on his face and when he played the trumpet they would kind of burst so he always carried a handkerchief and he wiped his face. But he dressed immaculately all the time. His hair was straight, like that Indian hair and he wore the best clothes and best shoes. Now he lives in Baton Rouge and he‟s getting to be very popular. Now [unintelligible] hung together, the white man of any popularity in any…

mulatto children to hang out with any unmixed black children. They had to hang out with the mulatto or else… never with unmixed black. This girl, his daughter, Daisy, falls in love with Guy Kelly and Guy Kelly is unmixed black and besides he‟s the most popular guy in Baton Rouge. The sheriff can‟t stand this [laugh]. He can‟t stand this. So he gets so upset he sends them both to Chicago. So that‟s where I get it… this guy came to Chicago and did some records he made with Gene Adler‟s father, [Unintelligible} Rag…
